context:
Goal: the install script stays proven where sessions really run it, and the records match CI.
Problem (rule): decision test-strategy-reset says the install script's checks run once, on macOS, but CI also runs them on Linux, and cloud sessions install on Linux.
Based on (measured): the Linux run takes 683 to 897 seconds, 53% of the checks-merge-install job; the test file itself says "Linux and macOS only".
Based on (read): the line protected one run of a suite tied to one system; nothing guards that now.
Departs from: decision test-strategy-reset line 23 says macOS only — a rewrites the line to Linux and macOS; b drops the Linux run.

options.gain: The record matches CI, and cloud installs stay proven.
options.how: The decision line becomes "Linux and macOS, since cloud sessions install on Linux"; CI stays as it is.
options.label: Keep both runs and fix the record (Recommended)
options.lose: 11 to 15 Linux minutes stay in each batch.

options.how: CI stops running the install checks on Linux, as the decision says.
options.label: Drop the Linux run
options.lose: Nothing proves the install path cloud sessions use.

ref: retrospective 15:53 CST Nov 12, CI audit; protocol outcomes-stale-decision-protocol
reply: Closed 16:03 CST: you picked a in the retrospective's chat at 15:55 CST (ruling R63): both runs stay and the decision line is rewritten to Linux and macOS.
title: The install script is tested on Linux too, though a decision says macOS only
why: The record says one thing and CI does another; only you can change the record.
